A conversation with a language model

Source: R/llm_native.R
llmchat.Rd

Sends a whole conversation (system, user and earlier assistant turns) to the route llmask would take, and returns the model's next reply. Use it when you manage the conversation yourself, for example to keep a multi-turn exchange or to give the model earlier answers as context. Unlike llmask() it adds nothing to the conversation (no help pages, no tools) and it never reads or writes the saved-answer cache.

Usage

llmchat(msgs, model = NULL, route = NULL, tmout = 120)

Arguments

msgs

A non-empty list of turns, each a list with two character scalars: role, one of "system", "user" or "assistant", and content, the text of that turn. The last turn is normally a "user" turn. Other elements of a turn are dropped.

model

Character scalar or NULL (the default): the model id to use (a value shaped like a key is refused, never sent). NULL uses the route's own choice: MORIE_LLM_MODEL for your own endpoint, OLLAMA_MODEL or the first pulled model for Ollama, the saved PROVIDER.model or the provider's default model (see llmprvd).

route

Character scalar or NULL (the default: the saved route, else the first that is set up). "auto" uses the automatic order and ignores a saved route; "own", "ollama" or a provider id insists on that one.

tmout

Numeric scalar, seconds to wait for each reply; default 120. With docs = TRUE the whole exchange gets at most three times this.

Value

A character scalar: the text of the model's reply.

Details

The route is resolved exactly as in llmrte. The turns are sent in the provider's own wire format (the OpenAI chat completions format for most providers, your own endpoint and Ollama; Anthropic's Messages API; Google's Gemini generateContent). One request is made, through the package's own libcurl binding, and waits at most tmout seconds.

Errors, before anything is sent: msgs is not a non-empty list of turns each with a single role among "system", "user" and "assistant" and a single non-missing character content; route = "hosted" or an unknown route; no route is set up (the message says what to set); the route has no model and model is not given. After sending: the server cannot be reached, rejects the key (HTTP 401 or 403), or answers with an error. The key is redacted from any error text a server echoes back.

See also

llmask for one question with the package help at hand.

Examples

old <- Sys.getenv(c("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", "OLLAMA_HOST"), unset = NA)
Sys.setenv(XDG_CONFIG_HOME = tempfile(), OLLAMA_HOST = "off")

# a conversation is a list of role/content turns
turns <- list(
  list(role = "system", content = "Answer in one sentence."),
  list(role = "user", content = "Name one type of survey weight.")
)
str(turns)
#> List of 2
#>  $ :List of 2
#>   ..$ role   : chr "system"
#>   ..$ content: chr "Answer in one sentence."
#>  $ :List of 2
#>   ..$ role   : chr "user"
#>   ..$ content: chr "Name one type of survey weight."

# a malformed turn is refused before anything is sent
try(llmchat(list("Name one type of survey weight.")))
#> Error : `msgs` must be a list of list(role = "system"|"user"|"assistant", content = text)

# with no route set up the error says what to set up
try(llmchat(turns, route = "ollama"))
#> Error : No language-model route is set up on this machine: bring your own key, or run a model locally:
#>   local Ollama: OLLAMA_HOST=off
#> `rmoriebricklayer config setup` walks through it.

for (v in names(old)) {
  if (is.na(old[[v]])) {
    Sys.unsetenv(v)
  } else {
    do.call(Sys.setenv, as.list(old[v]))
  }
}
if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# needs a key or a local model, and the network
Sys.setenv(ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "...")
llmchat(turns)
llmchat(c(turns, list(
  list(role = "assistant", content = "A design weight."),
  list(role = "user", content = "And a second one?")
)))
}
